subject: Readout: Dedicated performance Q&A + GPU trade-off summary
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Li <eli@finovatelabs.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 25 Apr 2028 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Readout: Dedicated performance Q&A + GPU trade-off summary

Ethan — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick readout and concrete next steps so we keep momentum on capacity planning for the pilot.

Key takeaways (from our discussions + notes):
- SLO targets: p50 latency target ~120–180ms; p95 <= 350ms for your median prompt length (~260 tokens). Streaming must maintain <= 250ms first-byte for interactive flows.
- Throughput / concurrency: baseline production target is ~80 sustained requests/sec with spikes to 160 req/sec during peak windows. Average tokens per request estimated 260; token throughput target ≈ 21k tokens/sec sustained.
- Reserved capacity ask: you want predictability for the first 6 months (no throttling above p95). We proposed a reserved pool; sizing options below.

GPU / sizing notes we discussed:
1) H100 (80GB) — best headroom for concurrency + long-context KV-cache uses; fewer nodes required for the same concurrent sessions, cleaner for streaming. Good fit if you want simpler ops and headroom for growth.
2) A100 (40/80GB variants) — very capable for bursty traffic; cost-effective at steady but higher unit count vs H100.
3) L4 / L40S — lower-cost option for smaller models or heavy quantization (int8); may require additional engineering to hit the p95 streaming target for worst-case long prompts.

Proposed pilot (minimal):
- 48-hour dedicated pilot using 2x H100 nodes (or 3x A100 if you prefer redundancy over single-node vertical scaling).
- Run our synthetic replay at your traffic profile (we'll provide the script) and a 2-hour production shadow run with 10% mirrored traffic.
- Deliverables: latency/throughput matrix, Kv-cache hit-rate, token-cost estimate, and recommended reserved throughput commit.

Attachments: I’ve attached a one-page GPU latency matrix and a draft mutual action plan.

Next steps / asks for you:
- Confirm which GPU family you want included in the pilot (H100 preferred for the initial run).
- Procurement: we need a PO or an email to start the dedicated capacity reservation (procurement@finovatelabs).
- Schedule a 30-min bench kickoff this week so our infra team can validate networking and test data.

I’ll loop Ben and Karthik on the bench details; Ben will own the pilot run and Karthik will own sizing calculations.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai
+1 415 555 0189

Subject: Re: Readout: Dedicated performance Q&A + GPU trade-off summary

Thanks Kimberly — helpful summary. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock pilot specs: 

1) Concurrency model: when you say 80 req/sec sustained, is that per virtual endpoint or across the entire reserved pool? Our traffic routing will split different customer profiles across endpoints; we need per-endpoint guarantees.

2) Streaming: for our UI team the first-byte threshold is critical. If we pilot with H100, what's the recommended batching strategy to avoid first-byte jitter at low qps?

3) Cost guardrails: procurement asked for an estimate of committed throughput (tokens/min) vs on-demand overage. Can you send a simple banded estimate we can show finance?

Finally, procurement asked whether Redwood can accept nested PO language around termination (they typically request 60–90 day notice for reserved-capacity contracts). Not a blocker for the pilot but want to flag.

We can confirm the PO for a timeboxed pilot once we have the cost bands and the kickoff slot. Would prefer the pilot to start Thursday (27th) if possible.

—Ethan

Head of Platform Engineering, Finovate Labs

Subject: Re: Readout: Dedicated performance Q&A + GPU trade-off summary

Ethan — quick technical clarifications and an action-ready sizing suggestion from our infra team: 

A) 80 req/sec reference is for the reserved pool (aggregate). If you need per-endpoint isolation, we recommend pinning endpoints to a subset of the pool and sizing per-endpoint guardrails — we can model that in the M-A-P.

B) Streaming first-byte jitter at low QPS: avoid batching for the first token. Our runtime supports adaptive batching: small requests (under 1 req/sec per model instance) are routed with batching disabled for the first token, then transient batching for subsequent tokens to preserve throughput. That pattern keeps first-byte under 200–250ms on H100 for 256–512 token streams.

C) Sizing proposal (practical):
- Conservative (recommended): 2 x H100 (80GB) dedicated nodes — handles 120 sustained req/sec with headroom for KV-cache and long-context scenarios. Good for p95 <= 350ms on 256–320 token workloads.
- Cost-balanced: 3 x A100 (40GB) — similar aggregate throughput but slightly higher operational complexity (more instances to manage).
- Cost-min: 4 x L4 (quantized int8) — only if you can accept higher p95 variance on long prompts and can run aggressive quantization.

D) Cost bands (very high-level):
- Pilot reserved (48h): fixed pilot fee + metered token usage. We’ll provide a short table that maps committed tokens/min -> estimated monthly spend if converted to a 12-month reserved commit. I'll attach that in the MAP and link to the drive.

E) Recommended next steps from infra:
- Kickoff bench: 30-min this Thursday to validate network and SSO.
- We run 48-hour replay on your sample dataset.
- We produce the perf matrix and recommend a commit (tokens/min and node count).

I attached the perf matrix we ran in a comparable customer pilot (see gpu-latency-matrix.pdf). I’ll follow up with the tokens/min -> $ bands as requested.

—Ben

Quick answers inline: 
- Per-endpoint guarantees: we can model per-endpoint SLAs in the MAP; for the pilot we’ll demonstrate aggregate pool behavior and then show how pinning affects per-endpoint throughput.
- First-byte jitter: Ben’s adaptive-batching approach is what we’ll enable for the pilot; it’s also the default in our streaming runtime for interactive endpoints.
- PO/termination language: our standard pilot paperwork is timeboxed and doesn’t require a long termination notice; enterprise reserved contracts support 60–90 day clauses and we can surface that to your legal/procurement in the follow-up.

Action items (owners):
- Ethan: confirm PO email or approval to proceed with a timeboxed pilot (Procurement).
- Procurement: please review the attached MAP and the pilot fee estimate and reply with any constraints.
- Ben: provide tokens/min -> $ bands and the short bench script link by EOD today.

If we get PO confirmation, we’ll reserve a pilot pool and circulate the bench invite + test plan.

Thanks — looking forward to the kickoff.
